title: Polynomial Equations and Inequalities
seo_title: Precalculus Polynomial Equations and Inequalities Worksheets (TEKS P.5I, P.5J)
standard_text: P.5I solve polynomial equations with real coefficients by applying a variety of techniques in mathematical and real-world problems; P.5J solve polynomial inequalities with real coefficients by applying a variety of techniques and write the solution set of the polynomial inequality in interval notation in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets for Texas TEKS P.5I and P.5J: solve polynomial equations by factoring and quadratic form, and polynomial inequalities with sign charts in interval notation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Factor, then set each factor equal to 0.
key_sub: Inequalities: zeros, then a sign chart.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To solve a polynomial equation, move everything to one side and factor: by a common factor, by grouping, by quadratic form, or with a known factor.
  • Set each factor equal to 0. Do not lose x = 0.
  • To solve a polynomial inequality, find the zeros, then make a sign chart: test one value in each interval.
  • A factor with an even power does not change the sign. Use [ ] for zeros when the inequality is ≤ or ≥.

Examples

Example

(x + 2)(x − 1)(x − 4) > 0

Zeros −2, 1, 4

Signs: −, +, −, +

Answer: (−2, 1) ∪ (4, ∞)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dropping x = 0x(x − 3) = 0 has two solutions.
Forgetting ±x2 = 9 gives 3 and −3.
Ignoring a squared factor(x − 2)2 keeps the same sign on both sides of 2.

faq.a: Solve polynomial equations with real coefficients by applying a variety of techniques in mathematical and real-world problems.

Solve polynomial inequalities with real coefficients by applying a variety of techniques and write the solution set of the polynomial inequality in interval notation in mathematical and real-world problems.

faq.q: Why test a value in each interval?
faq.a: A polynomial can only change sign at its zeros.

faq.q: Can the answer be a single point?
faq.a: Yes, for example (x − 2)² ≤ 0 gives only x = 2.

items.q: (x − 4) is a factor of x³ + 5x² − 16x − 80. Factor the polynomial completely.
items.e: Divide by (x − 4) to get x² + 9x + 20. Factor this quadratic: (x + 4)(x + 5). (x − 4)(x + 4)(x + 5).

items.q: The volume of a box is V(x) = x³ + 3x² + 2x. Its height is x + 1. What is the area of its base?
